facts.fact: CBOS Circular 7/2026 of 31 March 2026 sets binding minimum USSD rules and cites the Payment Systems Regulation 2013 and the 2020 mobile-payment financial institutions licensing regulation as its basis.
facts.system: Payment Systems Regulation 2013; Mobile Payment Financial Institutions Regulation 2020

facts.fact: The circular lets mobile-payment financial institutions and electronic payment providers licensed by the central bank offer USSD financial services alongside banks, on production of their CBOS licence certificate.
The circular obliges all payment service providers to connect their USSD platforms to the central national switch, 'when available', for interoperability; no deadline is set.

systems.owner: Central Bank of Sudan (regulator); banks, mobile-payment institutions and e-payment providers operate

facts.fact: The Regulation on Licensing and Organising Mobile Payment Financial Institutions 2020, issued under article 60(1) of the Banking Business Organisation Act 2004 (amended 2014), took effect on signature; the CBOS board approved it on 28 December 2020.
The 2020 regulation has the central bank licence companies, not banks, to run mobile payment and open e-money wallet accounts, with a rule that their names may not include 'bank'.

note: The regulation states no connection or interoperability requirement.
The circular sets AML, KYC and transfer-limit controls on existing channels; it does not say who may run payments or issue e-money.
Circular sets AML and KYC controls on transfers; it licenses no payment provider and requires no connection.
Central bank instructions are mentioned without being described as e-money or payment rules.
